name: brief-to-spec
title: Brief to Specification
purpose: Turn an ambiguous product or engineering brief into an implementation-ready specification.
inputs: goal, users, constraints, non-goals, acceptance signals
steps: separate facts, assumptions and open questions
define user-visible outcomes and explicit non-goals
turn each outcome into testable acceptance criteria
choose a minimal domain model and interfaces
record risks, dependencies and unresolved decisions
output: A short specification with context, scope, flows, interfaces, acceptance criteria and open questions.
checks: Every requirement has an observable acceptance signal.
Non-goals prevent scope creep.
Unknowns are labeled instead of invented.
example: A request for a browser export feature becomes a spec with supported formats, failure states and an export acceptance test.

name: technical-editing
title: Technical Editing
purpose: Improve technical prose without changing its claims, evidence or intended audience.
inputs: draft, audience, required terminology, length limit
steps: extract the draft's claims and evidence
remove vague subjects, filler and repeated context
tighten paragraph order around the reader's decision
preserve uncertainty and qualify unsupported claims
perform a terminology and consistency pass
output: An edited version plus a compact change log separating clarity edits from factual questions.
checks: No new facts are introduced.
Every claim still has the same strength as the draft.
Terms and acronyms are defined on first use.
example: A dense engineering update becomes a three-paragraph status note with a clear decision and known risks.

name: decision-memo
title: Decision Memo
purpose: Write a concise decision memo that makes alternatives and trade-offs auditable.
inputs: decision, context, options, constraints, evidence, owner
steps: state the decision and deadline first
separate must-have constraints from preferences
compare two or three viable options
make trade-offs explicit with evidence
record the chosen option, reversibility and follow-up owner
output: A decision memo with recommendation, alternatives, rationale, risks and next actions.
checks: The recommendation follows from stated criteria.
Rejected options have a reason.
The memo names who decides and what happens next.
example: A team choosing between a queue and a database receives a memo that compares durability, latency and operational cost.

name: meeting-actions
title: Meeting to Actions
purpose: Convert a meeting transcript or rough notes into accountable decisions and follow-ups.
inputs: transcript or notes, participants, date, project context
steps: distinguish decisions, proposals, questions and side discussion
attach each action to one owner and a due date when stated
preserve disagreements and unresolved questions
remove conversational filler while retaining evidence
return a decision log and an action list
output: A concise meeting record with decisions, owners, deadlines, dependencies and open questions.
checks: No speaker is assigned an action without evidence.
Unresolved items are not presented as decisions.
Dates and names remain faithful to the source.
example: A design review transcript becomes a decision log with three owners and two explicitly unresolved API questions.

name: resume-bullet
title: Resume Bullet Builder
purpose: Turn real work notes into concise, evidence-based resume bullets for a target role.
inputs: work notes, role description, tools used, outcomes, constraints
steps: identify the action, artifact, method and result
select language that matches the target role
quantify only values supported by the source
remove internal jargon and vague ownership
produce two lengths and flag missing evidence
output: Role-targeted bullets with a factual version and a shorter scan-friendly version.
checks: No invented metrics, titles or responsibilities.
Each bullet has a concrete artifact or outcome.
Technology names appear only when they explain the work.
example: A note about a rules engine becomes a bullet describing deterministic checks, evidence output and regression tests.

name: technical-article-outline
title: Technical Article Outline
purpose: Design a teachable structure for a technical article before drafting prose.
inputs: topic, reader level, central claim, examples, length
steps: state the reader problem and promised takeaway
sequence concepts from prerequisite to application
assign one job to each section
choose examples that test the central idea
add a verification section and a failure case
output: An article outline with section goals, examples, transitions and a fact-check list.
checks: The outline teaches one coherent idea.
Examples support rather than replace explanation.
The conclusion answers the opening reader problem.
example: A post about idempotent jobs gets sections for failure model, key design, retry example and verification.

name: paper-notes
title: Paper Notes
purpose: Create structured, critical notes from an academic paper without flattening uncertainty.
inputs: paper text, research question, reader purpose
steps: record the research question and claimed contribution
map data, method, assumptions and comparison baselines
separate reported results from interpretation
capture limitations and threats to validity
write a concise transfer-to-project section
output: A paper note with claim, method, evidence, limitations, reusable ideas and questions.
checks: Claims are tied to paper sections or figures.
Limitations are not omitted.
The note distinguishes the authors' result from the reader's inference.
example: A causal inference paper becomes notes on identification assumptions, estimand, robustness and reuse conditions.

name: evidence-matrix
title: Evidence Matrix
purpose: Organize sources so a research argument can be checked claim by claim.
inputs: research question, source set, candidate claims
steps: split the argument into atomic claims
assign the strongest source to each claim
record method, population, date and limitations
mark contradictory or indirect evidence
identify unsupported claims and next searches
output: A matrix linking claims to sources, evidence type, strength, caveats and gaps.
checks: One citation is not treated as proof of unrelated claims.
Evidence strength is explicit.
Contradictions remain visible.
example: A policy review separates an effect claim, mechanism claim and subgroup claim into three evidence rows.

name: claim-audit
title: Claim Audit
purpose: Audit a technical or research draft for unsupported, overstated or ambiguous claims.
inputs: draft, citations, source files, claim standard
steps: extract every externally checkable claim
classify each as fact, interpretation, estimate or recommendation
trace it to evidence or mark it unsupported
compare wording strength with evidence strength
return precise repairs without changing the thesis
output: A claim table with status, source, risk and suggested wording.
checks: Numbers have units, populations and time windows.
Causal language has causal support.
Recommendations are labeled as recommendations.
example: A sentence saying a model 'proves' an effect is softened when the study only reports an association.

name: literature-gap
title: Literature Gap Finder
purpose: Turn a set of papers into a defensible map of what is known, contested and missing.
inputs: paper summaries, topic boundary, comparison dimensions
steps: normalize papers by question, data, method and outcome
cluster repeated approaches and assumptions
mark disagreement and untested combinations
separate a genuine gap from an unsearched area
propose a narrow, testable next question
output: A gap map with evidence for each gap and a scoped research question.
checks: A gap is supported by the reviewed set.
Novelty is not claimed from absence alone.
The proposed question is feasible with stated data.
example: A review of demand forecasting identifies missing evaluation under promotion shocks rather than claiming the whole field is incomplete.

name: experiment-narrative
title: Experiment Narrative
purpose: Write a transparent result narrative from experiment logs, tables and plots.
inputs: hypothesis, setup, metrics, results, artifacts, limitations
steps: state the hypothesis and comparison first
describe only setup details needed to interpret results
report effect size and uncertainty before interpretation
connect each conclusion to an artifact
include failed runs and boundary conditions
output: A result section that separates observation, interpretation and limitation.
checks: Baseline and evaluation split are clear.
Metrics are defined before results.
The conclusion does not exceed the experiment.
example: A ranking experiment narrative reports offline gains, confidence intervals and the missing online validation.

name: citation-normalizer
title: Citation Normalizer
purpose: Normalize a mixed reference list and make citation fields consistent without fabricating metadata.
inputs: raw references, target style, available identifiers
steps: parse author, title, venue, year and identifier fields
resolve obvious formatting differences
mark missing fields and ambiguous matches
render the target style consistently
return an unresolved-items list
output: A normalized bibliography plus a list of fields requiring human verification.
checks: No missing DOI or year is invented.
Duplicate works are merged only with evidence.
In-text keys remain stable.
example: A list containing URLs, DOI strings and copied titles becomes one consistent bibliography with unresolved entries marked.

name: data-dictionary
title: Data Dictionary
purpose: Create a useful data dictionary that explains fields, lineage and safe usage.
inputs: schema, sample rows, source system, owners, business context
steps: inventory fields and data types
describe business meaning and units
record null, default and valid-value behavior
capture lineage, freshness and owner
add sensitive-data and join warnings
output: A field-level dictionary with examples, quality expectations and ownership.
checks: Names and descriptions agree with the schema.
Units and time zones are explicit.
Sensitive fields have handling guidance.
example: An events table dictionary records event_time timezone, deduplication key, late-arrival policy and owner.

name: metric-contract
title: Metric Contract
purpose: Define a metric so analysts, product teams and pipelines compute the same number.
inputs: metric name, business question, entities, event schema, time window
steps: define the entity and grain
write numerator, denominator and exclusions
specify time zone, late data and deduplication
add dimensions and guardrail metrics
define ownership, validation and change policy
output: A metric contract with formula, SQL-like pseudocode, examples and governance fields.
checks: The denominator is unambiguous.
A small example can be calculated by hand.
Changes have an owner and compatibility rule.
example: Weekly active users specifies user identity, qualifying event, calendar boundary and bot exclusion.

name: sql-review
title: SQL Review
purpose: Review analytical SQL for correctness, maintainability and cost without changing its intended result.
inputs: SQL, schema, expected grain, sample output, performance constraint
steps: state the output grain and join keys
check filters, null behavior and aggregation order
look for accidental fan-out and duplicate counting
review readability, partition use and expensive scans
return findings ordered by correctness risk
output: A review with severity, query location, explanation and a minimal fix or test.
checks: Every finding names the affected grain.
Performance claims reference a plan or known partition.
Refactoring suggestions preserve semantics.
example: A review catches a many-to-many join that doubles revenue before aggregation.

name: data-quality-plan
title: Data Quality Plan
purpose: Design practical checks and ownership for a dataset or pipeline.
inputs: dataset contract, failure history, consumers, freshness target
steps: list critical fields and invariants
choose completeness, validity, uniqueness and freshness checks
define thresholds and severity
map failures to owner and response
add a small representative fixture
output: A quality plan with checks, thresholds, alert policy, owners and test fixtures.
checks: Every check has a failure action.
Thresholds are tied to business impact.
The plan distinguishes warning from blocking failures.
example: An orders pipeline gets checks for unique order IDs, nonnegative totals, accepted currency codes and daily freshness.

name: experiment-design
title: Experiment Design
purpose: Turn a product or model question into a statistically defensible experiment plan.
inputs: hypothesis, unit, treatment, outcome, constraints, expected effect
steps: define estimand and randomization unit
choose primary outcome and guardrails
set inclusion, exclusion and exposure rules
plan power, duration and stopping policy
specify analysis, failure modes and interpretation
output: An experiment protocol with pre-registration fields and an analysis checklist.
checks: Treatment cannot leak into control.
Primary outcome is chosen before results.
Operational constraints are explicit.
example: A recommendation experiment specifies user-level assignment, purchase conversion, exposure minimum and a guardrail for latency.

name: dataset-card
title: Dataset Card
purpose: Document a dataset's provenance, composition, intended use and limitations.
inputs: dataset files, collection process, labels, license, known issues
steps: describe source and version
summarize population, fields and missingness
record collection and labeling choices
define intended and prohibited uses
list bias, privacy, drift and maintenance risks
output: A dataset card that lets a downstream user judge fitness before use.
checks: License and consent claims are sourced.
Known exclusions are visible.
Limitations are specific enough to test.
example: A text dataset card documents language mix, duplicate policy, PII removal and domain shift risk.

name: task-contract
title: Agent Task Contract
purpose: Specify an Agent task so success, permissions and failure handling are explicit.
inputs: user goal, available tools, data boundaries, success signal
steps: define the task outcome and non-goals
list allowed inputs, tools and side effects
set evidence and stop conditions
describe retries, escalation and human approval
create a small acceptance test set
output: A task contract with inputs, outputs, permissions, evidence, failure states and tests.
checks: The agent cannot silently expand scope.
Side effects require the named authorization.
Success is observable without judging prose style.
example: A repository documentation agent may read source and open a draft PR but cannot merge or alter credentials.

name: workflow-decomposer
title: Workflow Decomposer
purpose: Break a complex request into agent-sized steps with clear handoffs and dependencies.
inputs: goal, constraints, artifacts, tools, people
steps: separate research, transformation, decision and mutation work
order steps by information dependency
define artifact and owner at each handoff
mark parallel work and join conditions
add checkpoints for ambiguity and risk
output: A workflow graph or numbered plan with inputs, outputs, dependencies and checkpoints.
checks: Each step has one dominant purpose.
Handoffs name the artifact, not just a status.
High-impact mutations have a review gate.
example: A release workflow separates changelog drafting, test verification, approval and deployment instead of one giant agent prompt.

name: tool-interface
title: Tool Interface Designer
purpose: Design narrow, predictable tool interfaces for an Agent workflow.
inputs: agent task, external system, data model, error cases
steps: define the smallest useful operation
choose typed inputs and bounded outputs
separate preview from mutation
design idempotency and pagination behavior
specify errors, authorization and audit fields
output: A tool contract with schema, examples, error taxonomy and safety notes.
checks: A tool does not hide multiple unrelated actions.
Mutation and preview are distinguishable.
Errors are actionable and machine-readable.
example: A ticket tool exposes search, preview-update and apply-update separately with an idempotency key.

name: prompt-test-design
title: Prompt Test Design
purpose: Build a regression set that tests an Agent instruction against normal, ambiguous and adversarial inputs.
inputs: skill or prompt, target behavior, known failures, policy boundaries
steps: derive cases from intended behavior and exclusions
include minimal pairs that change one fact
add missing-input and conflicting-instruction cases
define expected behavior and evidence
tag tests by severity and automate stable checks
output: A prompt test matrix with fixtures, expected outcomes and evaluation notes.
checks: Tests cover refusal and clarification behavior.
Expected outcomes are behavior-based, not exact wording.
A failed test points to a specific instruction gap.
example: A summarization skill is tested with an empty source, contradictory dates, injected instructions and a normal report.

name: human-review-design
title: Human Review Design
purpose: Place human approval where an Agent's uncertainty or side effect warrants it.
inputs: workflow, risk classes, reversibility, reviewer role
steps: classify actions by impact and reversibility
set automatic, review-required and prohibited bands
define reviewer evidence and decision choices
record approval, rejection and override reasons
measure queue burden and false escalations
output: A review policy with gates, reviewer UI fields and escalation metrics.
checks: Review is required before irreversible effects.
The reviewer sees enough evidence to decide.
Low-risk work is not routed to a human by default.
example: An Agent may draft a refund automatically but requires approval before issuing money or changing account ownership.

name: agent-runbook
title: Agent Runbook
purpose: Create an operational runbook for observing, debugging and safely pausing an Agent workflow.
inputs: workflow contract, logs, tools, owners, incident history
steps: define health signals and useful trace fields
map common symptoms to likely causes
write safe pause, replay and rollback procedures
set escalation ownership and communication templates
add a post-incident learning loop
output: A runbook with dashboards, triage steps, recovery actions and escalation criteria.
checks: A responder can identify one run from its evidence.
Recovery steps state what must not be repeated.
Rollback does not rely on undocumented state.
example: A tool-call loop runbook defines max-step alerts, trace IDs, safe replay inputs and a kill switch.

name: bug-reproduction
title: Bug Reproduction
purpose: Turn a vague bug report into a minimal, repeatable reproduction package.
inputs: symptom, environment, logs, suspected inputs, expected behavior
steps: separate observed behavior from interpretation
record exact environment and preconditions
minimize the input while preserving failure
define expected and actual results
add a regression test shape and evidence request
output: A reproduction report with steps, fixture, logs, severity and a candidate regression test.
checks: Another engineer can reproduce without private context.
The minimal case still demonstrates the failure.
Environment assumptions are explicit.
example: A flaky parser bug becomes a five-line fixture with locale, input encoding and expected exception.

name: adr-writer
title: Architecture Decision Record
purpose: Record an architecture choice so future maintainers understand context and consequences.
inputs: problem, constraints, options, evidence, decision owner
steps: state the problem without prescribing the solution
list constraints and evaluation criteria
compare realistic alternatives
record the decision and consequences
define revisit triggers and status
output: An ADR with context, decision, alternatives, consequences and revisit conditions.
checks: The decision is dated and owned.
Consequences include costs and rejected benefits.
A future change has a trigger, not vague reconsideration.
example: An ADR chooses local storage over a hosted database for a privacy-first browser extension.

name: test-plan
title: Test Plan
purpose: Design a focused test plan from behavior, risk and system boundaries.
inputs: feature spec, interfaces, risk areas, environments
steps: map behavior to unit, integration and end-to-end layers
prioritize boundary and failure cases
define fixtures, mocks and cleanup
set exit criteria and evidence artifacts
identify tests that are expensive or flaky
output: A test matrix with cases, layer, owner, data and release gates.
checks: Critical behavior has a deterministic test.
Mocks do not erase the risk being tested.
Exit criteria are observable.
example: A file import feature gets parser unit tests, storage integration tests and one browser smoke test.

name: migration-plan
title: Migration Plan
purpose: Plan a data or API migration with compatibility, rollback and observability.
inputs: current state, target state, consumers, volume, downtime limit
steps: inventory readers, writers and invariants
choose expand, backfill and contract phases
define dual-read or dual-write behavior when needed
set validation, cutover and rollback checkpoints
plan cleanup and ownership after migration
output: A migration runbook with phases, commands, metrics, rollback and completion criteria.
checks: Old and new versions coexist safely during rollout.
Backfill is resumable and verifiable.
Rollback does not destroy the source of truth.
example: A nullable column migration adds the field, backfills in batches, validates parity and removes the old path later.

name: release-notes
title: Release Notes
purpose: Write release notes that tell users what changed, who is affected and what to do.
inputs: merged changes, issue links, known limitations, upgrade steps
steps: group changes by user outcome
separate new behavior, fixes and breaking changes
write migration or configuration steps
call out known limitations and rollback path
verify every claim against merged artifacts
output: Audience-focused release notes with upgrade guidance and issue references.
checks: Breaking changes are prominent.
Examples use the released interface.
Internal implementation details are omitted unless operationally relevant.
example: A version note explains a changed authentication default, migration command and affected configuration key.

name: incident-postmortem
title: Incident Postmortem
purpose: Produce a blameless incident record focused on system learning and durable actions.
inputs: timeline, alerts, logs, impact, response notes, contributing factors
steps: state impact and detection clearly
build a timestamped evidence-based timeline
separate trigger, contributing conditions and missed signals
identify what helped and what slowed response
assign small corrective actions with owners and due dates
output: A postmortem with impact, timeline, causes, response assessment and tracked actions.
checks: The narrative avoids individual blame.
Root cause is not reduced to the first visible error.
Actions change detection, prevention or recovery behavior.
example: A queue outage postmortem distinguishes a traffic spike from an unsafe retry policy and adds both capacity and alert actions.

name: email-reply
title: Email Reply
purpose: Draft a clear reply to a work or personal email while preserving the sender's intent and relationship.
inputs: original email, desired outcome, tone, deadline, facts that may be shared
steps: identify the request and hidden decision
separate facts from proposed wording
choose a direct opening and one clear next step
state constraints without sounding evasive
add a subject line and a shorter alternative
output: A ready-to-send reply plus one sentence explaining the requested action.
checks: The reply does not invent commitments or dates.
Questions are explicit rather than implied.
Tone matches the relationship and urgency.
example: A vague scheduling email becomes a reply with two available windows, a location and a confirmation request.

name: weekly-plan
title: Weekly Plan
purpose: Turn a mixed list of obligations into a realistic weekly plan with buffers.
inputs: tasks, fixed events, deadlines, available hours, energy constraints
steps: separate fixed commitments from movable work
estimate effort and identify dependencies
choose three priority outcomes
place deep work before routine work
reserve recovery and spillover time
output: A day-by-day plan with priorities, time blocks, fallback tasks and a review checkpoint.
checks: The plan fits the stated available hours.
Urgent work is not confused with important work.
A missed block has a recovery path.
example: A student week plan separates paper submission, coding practice and errands while leaving a buffer before the deadline.

name: document-to-checklist
title: Document to Checklist
purpose: Convert a policy, guide or long instruction into an actionable checklist without losing exceptions.
inputs: source document, audience, completion evidence, deadline
steps: extract obligations and conditional branches
rewrite each obligation as an observable action
preserve exceptions beside the action they modify
order actions by dependency
add evidence and escalation fields
output: A checklist with action, evidence, owner, condition and escalation path.
checks: Every checklist item can be marked complete from evidence.
Exceptions are visible at the decision point.
The checklist does not create requirements absent from the source.
example: A lab safety guide becomes a pre-run checklist with equipment checks, stop conditions and sign-off evidence.

name: personal-knowledge-cleanup
title: Personal Knowledge Cleanup
purpose: Organize notes into a small, searchable knowledge base without over-classifying personal information.
inputs: notes, tags or folders, retrieval goals, privacy boundaries
steps: group notes by retrieval question rather than date alone
merge exact duplicates and preserve conflicting versions
extract durable facts, decisions and pending questions
assign few stable tags and useful titles
mark sensitive notes and stale items
output: A cleaned note set with naming rules, tags, links and a review queue.
checks: Original meaning and uncertainty survive cleanup.
Sensitive content is not copied into summaries unnecessarily.
Tags improve retrieval instead of becoming a second taxonomy project.
example: Scattered study notes become topic pages with definitions, worked examples and a list of unresolved questions.

name: web-research-brief
title: Web Research Brief
purpose: Produce a compact, source-linked brief from a browsing task with clear freshness and uncertainty.
inputs: question, region, time window, trusted source types, decision to support
steps: rewrite the question into answerable subquestions
search primary or authoritative sources first
record publication date and scope for each source
separate verified facts from synthesis
end with a recommendation and remaining uncertainty
output: A brief with answer, source table, caveats and next search terms.
checks: Time-sensitive claims carry dates.
Sources directly support nearby claims.
The recommendation is labeled as an inference when appropriate.
example: A travel planning question becomes a brief comparing current opening hours, transit constraints and booking policies.

name: study-explainer
title: Study Explainer
purpose: Explain a difficult concept at the learner's level using checks for understanding rather than a lecture dump.
inputs: concept, learner level, known prerequisite, goal, preferred example
steps: diagnose the likely missing prerequisite
give a plain-language model before notation
work one example step by step
show one counterexample or common mistake
ask a short retrieval question and provide a self-check
output: A layered explanation with example, misconception warning and practice prompt.
checks: The explanation does not hide a necessary assumption.
The example is solved rather than merely named.
The self-check tests the target concept.
example: A probability explanation starts with sample space, computes one event and contrasts independence with mutual exclusivity.

name: ui-copy-to-component
title: UI Copy to Component
purpose: Turn a UI description into a small, accessible web component plan before writing code.
inputs: screen goal, content, states, interaction, framework, constraints
steps: identify the primary task and semantic elements
map content to component boundaries
define loading, empty, error and success states
choose keyboard and screen-reader behavior
specify responsive constraints and acceptance checks
output: A component plan with markup semantics, state table, props, interaction and test cases.
checks: Every interactive control has an accessible name.
Mobile behavior is explicit.
Error and empty states are designed, not left to defaults.
example: A dashboard filter description becomes a form with labeled controls, URL state and a no-results explanation.

name: webpage-debug
title: Webpage Debugging
purpose: Guide a systematic diagnosis of a broken webpage using observable browser evidence.
inputs: symptom, URL or local page, console output, network behavior, recent change
steps: reproduce in a clean viewport and record the symptom
classify layout, runtime, network or state failure
inspect the smallest relevant DOM, styles and console evidence
make one hypothesis-driven change at a time
verify desktop, mobile and refresh behavior
output: A debugging record with reproduction, evidence, hypothesis, fix and regression check.
checks: The fix is tied to evidence rather than visual guessing.
A successful reload is tested.
The report distinguishes site failure from environment failure.
example: A missing modal is traced from click event to console exception to a null selector, then covered by a smoke test.

name: accessibility-pass
title: Accessibility Pass
purpose: Review a web page for practical keyboard, semantic and visual accessibility issues.
inputs: page or component, target browsers, interaction flows, design constraints
steps: walk every flow with keyboard only
check landmarks, headings, labels, focus and announcements
inspect contrast, zoom and reduced-motion behavior
test errors and dynamic updates
prioritize fixes by blocked users and effort
output: An accessibility findings list with severity, element, reproduction and repair guidance.
checks: Findings include a user impact.
Keyboard and screen-reader issues are distinguished.
The review verifies fixes rather than only listing rules.
example: A dialog review catches focus escaping to the page, a missing label and an error message not announced.

name: responsive-layout-review
title: Responsive Layout Review
purpose: Turn screenshots or a page brief into responsive layout rules that remain stable across viewports.
inputs: design or screenshots, target widths, content extremes, existing CSS
steps: identify fixed, fluid and intrinsic dimensions
find likely wrap and overflow boundaries
define layout changes at content-driven breakpoints
test long labels, empty states and zoom
write CSS-level acceptance checks
output: A responsive layout note with constraints, breakpoints, overflow policy and test cases.
checks: Breakpoints respond to content rather than device names alone.
No state depends on hidden clipping.
Long text and keyboard focus remain visible.
example: A card grid plan defines minmax tracks, a one-column fallback and behavior for a long project name.

name: browser-automation-plan
title: Browser Automation Plan
purpose: Design a reliable browser automation flow before implementing selectors and actions.
inputs: user flow, target pages, authentication boundary, artifacts, failure cases
steps: define the business outcome and safe stopping point
choose stable semantic selectors before CSS paths
separate navigation, assertion and mutation steps
plan screenshots, traces and cleanup
add retry limits and manual handoff conditions
output: An automation plan with selectors, assertions, artifacts, retries and authorization gates.
checks: The flow never guesses destructive confirmation.
Assertions prove state before the next mutation.
Authentication and secrets stay outside page text.
example: A form-filling flow checks the account and draft state before submitting, then saves a confirmation screenshot.

name: frontend-file-map
title: Frontend File Map
purpose: Explain an unfamiliar frontend repository so a contributor can find the correct files safely.
inputs: repository tree, package scripts, routes, entry points, target change
steps: locate build entry, routes and shared UI boundaries
trace the target screen from route to data to component
record state ownership and styling conventions
identify tests, fixtures and generated files
return a smallest-change map with unknowns
output: A repository map with relevant files, data flow, conventions and safe edit boundaries.
checks: Generated and source files are distinguished.
The map cites inspected paths.
Unknown ownership is stated rather than guessed.
example: A request to change a settings panel maps route, loader, form component, validation schema and existing tests.
